# Aggressive always-long TQQQ volatility target — development report

**Slug:** `tqqq-vol-target-aggressive`
**Window:** 2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29 (development only; 2024-2026 never loaded
or inspected)
**Harness:** `research/bt.py`, 1-minute regular-session marks, next-open fills,
2% band, 1 bp headline; 5 bp and 10 bp sensitivity. Long-only, weights ≥ 0,
sum ≤ 1.
**Files:** `HYPOTHESIS.md` (pre-registration), `strategy.py`, `result.json`.

---

## Verdict

**Pass on the development bar, and on the mandate's DD < 60% target.** At 1 bp
the promoted cell `rv20_t080` makes **40.16% CAGR / 57.77% max DD / 1.068
Sharpe**, versus the TQQQ bar of **36.72% / 82.29% / 0.82**. It still passes at
5 bp (**39.06% / 58.26% / 1.048**) and 10 bp (**37.71% / 58.87% / 1.023**).
Daily-close marks give 39.90% / 56.20% / 1.053.

The qualification is material. The CAGR edge is **+3.44 pp**, but it is not
broad alpha: the strategy **underperforms TQQQ in every bull year** (2016,
2017, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2023) and wins in 2018 and 2022. Excluding the best
year (2023) the CAGR falls to **24.57%**, below the absolute bar, though still
above TQQQ's 18.59% ex-2023. The strategy is best described as **risk-managed
TQQQ beta with a crash brake**, not as a new return source. The holdout is a
genuine coin-flip: it needs **30.51% CAGR** over 2024-2026 to match the full
37.54% bar, and its 75.8% average exposure and 0.795 monthly up-capture put it
right around that level.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **CAGR** | **40.16%** | **39.06%** | **37.71%** | 36.15% | 36.72% |
| **Max DD** | **57.77%** | **58.26%** | **58.87%** | 82.29% | 82.29% |
| **Sharpe** | **1.068** | **1.048** | **1.023** | 0.801 | 0.82 |
| Sortino | 1.495 | 1.466 | 1.430 | — | — |
| Calmar (CAGR/DD) | 0.695 | 0.671 | 0.641 | 0.439 | 0.446 |
| Volatility | 38.75% | 38.75% | 38.75% | 66.55% | — |

| Fills | 1,645 | 1,645 | 1,647 | 1 | — |

| Ending equity ($100k) | $1,481,124 | $1,391,328 | $1,287,160 | $1,175,283 | — |

`bt.stats` reports `exposure` ≈ 100% because BIL is an asset; `tqqq_exposure`
above is the economic TQQQ weight. The benchmark measured on the same 1-minute
panel is 36.15% / 82.29% / 0.801; the task's reference bar is 36.72% / 82.29% /
0.82. The candidate beats both. The daily-close benchmark is 35.98% / 81.68% /
0.799.

## 1. What the strategy does

Let `C_t` be TQQQ's adjusted daily close, `r_t = ln(C_t/C_{t-1})`, and
`σ_t = sqrt(252)·std(r_{t-19..t})`.

```
base_t  = clip(0.80 / σ_t, 0, 1)
hi15_t  = max(C_{t-14..t})
dd15_t  = 1 - C_t / hi15_t
brake_t = clip(1 - (dd15_t - 0.06) / (0.12 - 0.06), 0.25, 1)
w_t     = EMA_3(base_t · brake_t)        # span 3, causal
BIL_t   = 1 - w_t
```

The weight is set from the close of session `t` and filled at the open of
`t+1`. There is no moving-average regime, no slow trend gate, no stop-loss and
no shorting. The 3-session EMA is a turnover control: in the exploratory
raw-target run it reduced traded notional from 1,256× to 874× start equity and
raised the 10 bp CAGR from 35.57% to 37.71%; it is not a signal.

The brake is a **fast drawdown scaler**, not a binary crash stop. It is full at
a 15-session drawdown of 6% or less, falls linearly to 0.25 at 12%, and stays at
0.25 beyond. It is active often: the average weight is **75.8%**, the strategy is
at ≥99% only **46.3%** of sessions, and below 50% **26.4%** of sessions. That is
the "aggressive" shape: fully invested in calm tapes, hard cut in drawdowns.

## 2. Yearly returns

Measured from session-end equity on the 1-minute panel. The 2016 base is the
first session of the archive.

| Year | Strategy | TQQQ | Difference | Avg TQQQ weight |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016 | +17.5% | +18.6% | −1.1 pp | 82.9% |
| 2017 | +103.6% | +118.3% | −14.7 pp | 96.7% |
| 2018 | **−15.1%** | −19.6% | +4.5 pp | 67.6% |
| 2019 | +92.6% | +133.1% | −40.5 pp | 85.0% |
| 2020 | +100.7% | +109.6% | −8.9 pp | 71.1% |
| 2021 | +40.5% | +83.0% | −42.5 pp | 82.0% |

| 2023 | +154.0% | +198.4% | −44.4 pp | 80.4% |

The shape is exactly a crash-avoidance payoff: give up 1–44 pp in bull years,

The strategy loses to TQQQ in the two bull subperiods and wins by 36.8 pp CAGR

## 3. Pre-registered grid and plateau

All cells use the same brake (`H=15`, 6–12%, floor 0.25) and EMA-3 smoothing.
The primary `rv20_t080` was fixed before the run as the lowest target in the
mandated 0.8–1.0 range, i.e. the most conservative point and the one that
prioritises DD < 60%.

**Plateau:** 7 of 8 cells pass the formal program bar; 6 of the 7 cut cells pass

1-minute marks but 59.92% on daily closes, so the DD constraint is
mark-frequency-sensitive at the top of the range.

The primary is the **best CAGR cell of the 8-cell grid**. That is a warning
sign and is disclosed in `result.json` (`primary_is_best_cagr: true`). The
defence is that the 0.90 cell is only 0.77 pp behind and also passes both tests,
and the 0.90/1.00 cells still pass the formal program bar; the result is not a
single-cell artifact. The DD < 60% margin, however, is target-sensitive.

## 4. Neighbour robustness

## 5. Is the target just leverage?

No weight exceeds 1, so the strategy is not levered above TQQQ. The average
TQQQ weight is 75.8%. The constant controls show that leverage/constant
exposure cannot reproduce the result:

| Constant TQQQ | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 60% | 27.94% | 60.78% | 0.82 |
| 70% | 30.71% | 67.44% | 0.81 |
| 80% | 33.10% | 73.02% | 0.81 |
| 85% | 33.68% | 76.05% | 0.80 |
| 90% | 35.41% | 77.88% | 0.81 |
| 95% | 35.74% | 80.38% | 0.80 |
| 100% | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 |

Every constant fails the CAGR bar; every constant of 60% or more has a
drawdown above 60%. The **matched constant** at the primary's average weight
(75.8%) makes **31.93% / 69.49% / 0.800** on daily marks, versus the strategy's
**39.91% / 56.20% / 1.053**. Same average exposure, 8.0 pp more CAGR and 13.3 pp
less DD: the timing, not the exposure, is the edge.

The honest comparison to the moderate-target sibling is less flattering. A
supplementary run of a 0.45 target with no brake (the earlier
`always-long-vol-target` design) makes **39.47% / 58.94% / 0.999** with 79.5%
average exposure on this harness. The aggressive candidate is only **+0.69 pp
CAGR and −1.17 pp DD** better at 1 bp, and is slightly worse at 10 bp (37.71% vs
38.23% for the sibling's frozen result). The high nominal target is **not** a
large improvement over a moderate vol target. Its distinct feature is the shape
— full exposure in calm tapes, a hard cut in drawdowns — not a new risk/return
frontier.

## 6. Is the crash cut the real edge?

The clean decomposition uses the same target, estimator and EMA-3 smoothing:

| Variant | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | TQQQ expo |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| No cut (`rv20_t080_nocut`) | 38.28% | 78.33% | 0.854 | 95.5% |
| **Fast drawdown brake** | **40.16%** | **57.77%** | **1.068** | **75.8%** |
| Binary cut at 12% DD | 36.61% | 65.23% | 0.945 | 81.7% |
| Vol-acceleration cut only | 41.24% | 77.04% | 0.913 | 92.6% |

The brake's **robust contribution is the drawdown reduction: −20.6 pp** at a
small CAGR cost/benefit that depends on the smoothing. With the pre-registered
EMA-3 it adds +1.88 pp CAGR; without the EMA the raw no-cut control makes
39.54% / 78.36% and the raw cut 39.39% / 58.78%, i.e. the cut costs −0.15 pp
CAGR for −19.6 pp DD. The truth is: **the cut is the real DD edge; it is not a
reliable CAGR engine.** The CAGR edge over buy-and-hold comes mainly from the
vol target's modest de-risking in the worst vol states, and from avoiding the
2022 loss.

The cut-shape rivals confirm that the drawdown state is special. A **binary**
cut at 12% is worse on both axes (36.61% / 65.23%): it re-enters too early and
whipsaws. A **vol-acceleration-only** cut raises CAGR to 41.24% but leaves the
DD at 77.04%: it catches the acute 2020 spike but not the slow 2022 grind. The
continuous 15-session drawdown brake is what handles both.

## 7. Placebos, causality and performance cuts

**Placebos (daily marks, 500 circular shifts of the daily weight path).** The
real daily path makes 39.91% / 56.20% / 1.053. The matched constant makes
31.93% / 69.49% / 0.800. The shift distribution has mean CAGR 28.27% (p05
16.45%, p50 28.22%, p95 41.13%), mean DD 73.32% (p50 73.77%) and median Sharpe
0.732. **6.6%** of shifts beat the real CAGR; **0.0%** beat both the real CAGR
and the real DD. The alignment of the weights with returns matters, and the DD
improvement is far outside the placebo distribution.

**Lag placebo.** Delaying the weight path by 5 sessions gives 35.26% / 54.99%
(Sharpe 0.928); 20 sessions gives 23.90% / 68.17% (0.684); 60 sessions gives
25.18% / 69.40% (0.688). A 5-day lag still works because the brake is a slow
state; 20+ days loses the edge. The signal is not a same-day artifact.

**Causal truncation.** Rebuilding the weights on panels truncated at
2018-12-31, 2020-03-12 11:07, 2021-12-31 and 2022-09-13 gives **0.0 maximum
absolute difference** on both the minute and daily panels at all four cuts. This
is the bug that rejected the earlier always-long vol-target (it used the
panel's last timestamp to set the daily signal end, so a mid-day truncation
changed the same morning's weights); this implementation loads the daily signal
only through the session **before** the panel's last session, so the truncated
panel cannot change any pre-cut weight.

**Performance cuts.**

| Cut | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Ex-best year (2023, +154.0%) | 24.57% | 56.36% | 0.792 |
| Ex-2020 | 28.30% | 56.36% | 0.891 |
| Ex-2022 | 51.84% | 37.96% | 1.330 |
| Ex-best 20 sessions | 16.22% | 70.44% | 0.592 |
| Start 2017-01-03 | 43.23% | 57.77% | 1.113 |
| Start 2018-01-02 | 35.03% | 57.77% | 0.943 |

The ex-best-year and ex-best-20 rows are the weak points. The strategy gives up
a lot in strong up years and depends on participating in the 2023 recovery and
on a small number of large up days. The start-2018 CAGR is below the absolute
36.72% bar, but it still beats TQQQ's 27.44% / 81.7% over 2018-2023. The
drawdown improvement is robust across all cuts; the CAGR is not.

## 8. Holdout arithmetic and honest verdict

The dev multiple is 14.81× over 7.984 years. Matching the full 2016-2026 TQQQ
bar (37.54% CAGR, 31.27× over 10.801 years) requires **2.111× over the 2.806
holdout years, i.e. 30.51% CAGR**. The strategy's 75.8% average exposure and
0.795 monthly up-capture imply roughly 30–31% in a holdout where TQQQ compounds
near 39.5%, before any brake cost. That is **right at the required level** — a
real chance, not a comfortable margin.

What would make the holdout fail:

- a strong, low-drawdown bull market in which the brake's 1–44 pp annual
  give-up is not repaid by a crash (the 2021 problem: +40.5% vs +83.0%);
- another 2023-like recovery where the strategy participates but lags TQQQ by
  44 pp;
- a repeat of the 2018 start: 35.03% dev CAGR is below the absolute bar.

What would make it succeed:

- a 2022-like drawdown, where the strategy loses about half of TQQQ's loss;
- a 2020-like crash, where the brake's 31% loss vs TQQQ's 70% is worth years of
  beta;
- a holdout with TQQQ above ~40%, where the 75.8% average exposure alone can
  clear 30.5%.

**Bottom line.** This is a valid, causal, mandate-compliant strategy that
passes the development bar and the DD < 60% target at 1, 5 and 10 bp. It is
**not** evidence that aggressive 0.8–1.0 vol targets are superior: the nominal
target is nearly flat from 0.70 to 0.85, the realised exposure is 75.8%, and the
result is only ~0.7 pp CAGR better than a moderate 0.45 target. The crash brake
is the real DD edge, worth about 20 pp of drawdown; the CAGR edge is modest and
concentrated in 2022–2023. Promote it to the one-shot holdout as a
**risk-managed TQQQ beta / crash-hedge**, with the expectation that it will
underperform in a strong bull and outperform in a drawdown. Do not expect the
40% dev CAGR to repeat.

# Hypothesis and pre-registration — `tqqq-vol-target-aggressive`

**Status:** frozen for the development evaluation. This file is written **before**
the final grid run; every number in `report.md` comes from the exact grid and
rules below.
**Development window:** 2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29 only. The 2024-01-02 →
2026-10-23 holdout is not loaded, inspected or used for selection.
**Universe:** TQQQ (long), BIL (cash). QQQ is used only for benchmark context,
never as a signal.
**Execution:** daily target set at session close `t`, filled at the open of
`t+1`; 2% band; 1 bp headline, 5 bp and 10 bp sensitivity. Long-only,
weights ≥ 0, sum ≤ 1. Headline marks are 1-minute; daily marks are a
cross-check.

## 1. Mechanism

TQQQ is a 3× daily-reset fund. Its compound return is taxed by realised
variance and its drawdowns are amplified by the daily reset. The mandate is the
**aggressive end** of the always-long volatility-target family: hold TQQQ at
all times, sized inversely to a causal realised-vol estimate with a high
nominal target (0.8–1.0 annualised), and add only a **fast crash cut** — no slow
trend gate, no moving-average regime, no discretionary flat.

The economic bet is asymmetric:

1. In calm and normal-vol tapes, TQQQ's drift is large relative to its variance
   and the strategy should be close to fully invested. A high target preserves
   that participation.
2. In acute high-vol states the 3× reset drag and gap risk are largest; scaling
   down is cheap insurance.
3. A fast drawdown brake is needed because TQQQ's worst damage (2020Q1, 2022)
   is a *path* of accelerating losses, not a single vol spike. The brake cuts
   when price is meaningfully below its recent high and restores when the
   recent high is recovered.

The honest prior is that the nominal target is **not** leverage: weights are
capped at 1. The average realised exposure will be below 1 and may end up close
to a much lower vol target. The report therefore separates (a) the value of vol
timing, (b) the value of the crash brake, and (c) the value of the average
exposure itself (matched constant and 80–100% constant controls).

## 2. Exact rules

Let `C_t` be TQQQ's adjusted daily close, `r_t = ln(C_t/C_{t-1})`.

**Volatility estimators** (computed through the close of session `t`, strictly
causal):

- `RV_N`: annualised sample standard deviation (`ddof=1`) of the last `N` daily
  log returns, `sqrt(252)·std(r_{t-N+1..t})`. Primary.
- `PARK_N`: Parkinson range estimator over the last `N` sessions,
  `sqrt(252/(4 ln 2)·mean(ln(H_i/L_i)²))`, adjusted daily high/low. Rival.
- `EWMA_λ`: RiskMetrics variance recursion with `λ = 0.94`, annualised. Rival.

**Base position:**

```
base_t = clip(target_vol / sigma_t, 0, 1)
```

**Fast crash brake:**

```
hi15_t  = max(C_{t-14..t})
dd15_t  = 1 - C_t / hi15_t
brake_t = clip(1 - (dd15_t - 0.06) / (0.12 - 0.06), 0.25, 1)
```

So the brake is full at a drawdown of 6% or less, declines linearly to a floor
of 0.25 at a 12% drawdown, and stays at the floor beyond. It uses only the
completed daily bar and is applied from the next session's open.

**Target:**

```
raw_t = base_t · brake_t
w_t   = EMA_3(raw_t)          # span 3, adjust=False, causal
b_t   = 1 - w_t               # BIL
```

The 3-session EMA is a turnover control, not a signal: it reduces traded
notional at the 2% band. It is applied to the final target, so the decay is
causal.

If `sigma_t` is missing or non-positive, `w_t = 0`; with the 2015 prehistory this
can only happen in the first few sessions of 2016, not in the evaluation window.
There is no trend filter, no slow moving average, no volatility-of-volatility
term, no stop-loss and no shorting.

## 3. Pre-registered grid (8 cells)

The brake is fixed at the values above for every cell. The grid spans the
mandated target range and two rival estimator families. **Primary:
`rv20_t080`** — the lowest target in the mandated 0.8–1.0 range, chosen a priori
as the most conservative point and the one that prioritises the DD < 60%
constraint. It is not chosen from the results. The report discloses that it is
the best CAGR cell of the pre-registered grid; the out-of-grid 0.70 and 0.75
targets are marginally better on both axes and are disclosed but not promoted,
to avoid selecting the best out-of-grid cell on the evaluation window.

| id | estimator | lookback | target vol | brake |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| **`rv20_t080` (primary)** | **RV** | **20** | **0.80** | **on** |
| `rv20_t090` | RV | 20 | 0.90 | on |
| `rv20_t100` | RV | 20 | 1.00 | on |
| `rv10_t080` | RV | 10 | 0.80 | on |
| `rv60_t080` | RV | 60 | 0.80 | on |
| `park20_t080` | PARK | 20 | 0.80 | on |
| `ewma_t080` | EWMA 0.94 | 20 | 0.80 | on |
| `rv20_t080_nocut` | RV | 20 | 0.80 | **off** |

**Plateau rule:** the primary is promoted only if (a) it passes the program bar
(CAGR > 36.72%, DD < 82.29%), (b) it meets the mandate's DD < 60% target, (c) at
least 5 of the 7 cut cells pass the program bar, and (d) the 0.9 and 1.0 targets
are not catastrophic (both still pass the program bar, or are within 1 pp CAGR
of it). If only the lowest-exposure cell passes, that is reported as a
near-control failure, not a plateau.

## 4. Out-of-grid diagnostics (not used for selection)

- **No-cut control:** the same target and estimator without the brake. This is
  the cleanest test of whether the crash cut is the real edge.
- **Constant TQQQ blends:** 60, 70, 80, 85, 90, 95 and 100% TQQQ, remainder BIL,
  rebalanced daily under the same 2% band. The 80–100% band is the direct
  "is this just leverage?" control.
- **Matched constant:** a constant TQQQ weight equal to the primary's realised
  average weight. Same average exposure, no timing.
- **Brake neighbours:** high lookback 10/15/20/30; start 0.04/0.05/0.06/0.08;
  end 0.12/0.15/0.20/0.25; floor 0.00/0.10/0.20/0.25/0.30/0.40. Reported as a
  plateau, not a search for the best cell.
- **Cut-shape rivals:** a binary cut at a 12% drawdown (floor 0.25) and a
  volatility-acceleration cut (`RV5 > 1.5·RV20` and `RV5 > 0.70`, weight 0.30).
- **Estimator neighbours:** RV5, RV120, PARK10, PARK60, RV10+RV60 blend, and
  EWMA with a longer span.
- **Smoothing neighbours:** raw (no EMA), EMA span 2 and 5.
- **Lag placebo:** the primary weight path delayed by 5, 20 and 60 sessions.
- **Circular-shift placebo:** the primary daily weight path shifted by a random
  offset (uniform in `[60, n−60]`, 500 draws), preserving the exact weight
  distribution, turnover and autocorrelation while destroying alignment with
  returns.

## 5. Cut tests

- **Causal truncation:** rebuild the weights on panels truncated at 2018-12-31,
  2020-03-12 11:07, 2021-12-31 and 2022-09-13; every pre-cut weight must be
  identical to the full-panel weight.
- **Performance cuts:** drop the best calendar year, drop 2020, drop 2022, drop
  the best 20 sessions, and start in 2017 and 2018.
- **Subperiods:** 2016–2019, 2020–2021, 2022–2023, plus yearly returns.
- **Episodes:** 2018Q4, the COVID crash and recovery, the 2022 bear and the 2023
  recovery.

## 6. Pass criterion and interpretation

The formal bar is **dev CAGR > 36.72% and max DD < 82.29%** on 1-minute marks at
1 bp. The mandate's tighter target is **DD < 60%**. A pass on CAGR with DD
between 60% and 82% is reported as a partial pass, not a clean one.

The report must answer three questions explicitly:

1. **Is the target just leverage?** No weight exceeds 1; the 80–100% constant
   controls and the matched constant answer whether the average exposure alone
   explains the result.
2. **Is the crash cut the real edge?** The no-cut, binary-cut and
   vol-acceleration-cut rows separate the CAGR effect from the DD effect.
3. **Is the result a plateau or a single cell?** The 8-cell grid plus the brake
   neighbours and the two estimator families answer this.

## 7. Data and causality notes

- The 1-minute archive starts 2016-01-04. The daily yahoo archive starts
  2015-01-02 and is used only to warm the volatility and drawdown estimators
  before the first 1-minute session; every decision in the evaluation window
  uses data through that session's close only.
- Daily OHLC are adjusted by `adjclose/close` (the same factor convention as
  `bt.load_1m`). Execution and marks use the 1-minute panel.
- `build_weights` loads the daily signal only through the **session before the
  panel's last session**, and maps session `j`'s target from the signal at
  `j−1` to session `j`'s bars. No same-day close enters that session's weight.
  The last bar of session `j−1` carries session `j`'s target so the 2% band and
  the next-open fill happen at the session boundary.
- No full-sample statistic enters the weight: every estimator is a trailing
  window or a recursion seeded only with past data.

## 1. What the strategy does

Let `C_t` be TQQQ's adjusted daily close, `r_t = ln(C_t/C_{t-1})`, and
`σ_t = sqrt(252)·std(r_{t-19..t})`.

```
base_t  = clip(0.80 / σ_t, 0, 1)
hi15_t  = max(C_{t-14..t})
dd15_t  = 1 - C_t / hi15_t
brake_t = clip(1 - (dd15_t - 0.06) / (0.12 - 0.06), 0.25, 1)
w_t     = EMA_3(base_t · brake_t)        # span 3, causal
BIL_t   = 1 - w_t
```

The weight is set from the close of session `t` and filled at the open of
`t+1`. There is no moving-average regime, no slow trend gate, no stop-loss and
no shorting. The 3-session EMA is a turnover control: in the exploratory
raw-target run it reduced traded notional from 1,256× to 874× start equity and
raised the 10 bp CAGR from 35.57% to 37.71%; it is not a signal.

The brake is a **fast drawdown scaler**, not a binary crash stop. It is full at
a 15-session drawdown of 6% or less, falls linearly to 0.25 at 12%, and stays at
0.25 beyond. It is active often: the average weight is **75.8%**, the strategy is
at ≥99% only **46.3%** of sessions, and below 50% **26.4%** of sessions. That is
the "aggressive" shape: fully invested in calm tapes, hard cut in drawdowns.

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Daily signal data

def load_daily(end: str | pd.Timestamp | date = DEV_END) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Adjusted TQQQ daily OHLC, read only through `end` (inclusive)."""
    end_day = pd.Timestamp(end).date()
    key = end_day
    if key in _DAILY_CACHE:
        return _DAILY_CACHE[key]
    read_to = end_day + timedelta(days=1)
    df = pd.read_parquet(
        DATA / "TQQQ-1d-yahoo.parquet",
        columns=["date", "open", "high", "low", "close", "adjclose"],
        filters=[("date", "<", read_to)],
    )
    df["date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["date"])
    df = df.sort_values("date").drop_duplicates("date").reset_index(drop=True)
    factor = (df["adjclose"] / df["close"]).to_numpy(float)
    for col in ("open", "high", "low", "close"):
        df[col] = df[col].to_numpy(float) * factor
    df = df.set_index("date")[["open", "high", "low", "close"]]
    df = df.loc[df.index <= pd.Timestamp(end_day)]
    _DAILY_CACHE[key] = df
    return df


def estimate_vol(df: pd.DataFrame, kind: str, window: int) -> pd.Series:
    """Causal annualised volatility, all data through each row's close."""
    lr = np.log(df["close"]).diff()
    if kind == "rv":
        return lr.rolling(window, min_periods=window).std(ddof=1) * np.sqrt(252.0)
    if kind == "park":
        hl2 = np.log(df["high"] / df["low"]) ** 2
        var = hl2.rolling(window, min_periods=window).mean() / (4.0 * np.log(2.0))
        return np.sqrt(var * 252.0)
    if kind == "ewma":
        var = lr.pow(2).ewm(alpha=0.06, adjust=False, min_periods=window).mean()
        return np.sqrt(var * 252.0)
    if kind == "blend":
        a = estimate_vol(df, "rv", 10)
        b = estimate_vol(df, "rv", 60)
        return np.sqrt(0.5 * a.pow(2) + 0.5 * b.pow(2))
    raise ValueError(f"unknown estimator {kind}")


def daily_weights(df: pd.DataFrame, p: dict) -> pd.Series:
    """Daily TQQQ target weight, computed at each session's close."""
    vol = estimate_vol(df, p["estimator"], int(p["window"]))
    base = np.minimum(float(p["target"]) / vol.to_numpy(float), 1.0)
    base = np.where(np.isfinite(base), base, 0.0)
    if p.get("cut", True):
        hi = df["close"].rolling(int(p["dd_window"])).max()
        dd = 1.0 - df["close"] / hi
        brake = np.clip(1.0 - (dd.to_numpy(float) - p["dd_start"])
                        / (p["dd_end"] - p["dd_start"]), p["dd_floor"], 1.0)
        brake = np.where(np.isfinite(brake), brake, 1.0)
    else:
        brake = np.ones(len(df))
    w = pd.Series(base * brake, index=df.index)
    if p.get("smooth", 0):
        w = w.ewm(span=int(p["smooth"]), adjust=False).mean()
    return w


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Weight construction (required entry point)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def build_weights(ts, o, c, params: dict | None = None) -> np.ndarray:
    """Panel -> (n, 3) TQQQ/BIL weights, causal and next-open ready.

    The signal is loaded only through the session before the panel's last
    session, so a truncated panel cannot change any pre-cut weight.  Session
    j's target is the signal at j-1; the last bar of session j-1 carries it so
    the fill happens at the first bar's open of session j.
    """
    p = dict(BASE)
    if params:
        p.update(params)
    ts = pd.DatetimeIndex(ts)
    if len(ts) == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 3))
    dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    sess = pd.DatetimeIndex(pd.to_datetime(dates[last]))
    signal_end = sess[-2] if len(sess) > 1 else sess[0] - pd.Timedelta(days=1)
    df = load_daily(signal_end)
    wd = daily_weights(df, p)
    at = wd.reindex(sess, method="ffill")
    prev = at.shift(1)
    before = wd[wd.index < sess[0]]
    prev.iloc[0] = float(before.iloc[-1]) if len(before) else 0.0
    counts = last - first + 1
    w_bar = np.repeat(prev.to_numpy(float), counts)
    w_bar = np.roll(w_bar, -1)
    w_bar[-1] = prev.to_numpy(float)[-1]
    w_bar = np.clip(w_bar, 0.0, 1.0)
    W = np.zeros((len(ts), 3))
    W[:, 1] = w_bar
    W[:, 2] = 1.0 - w_bar
    return W


def daily_panel_weights(tsd, p: dict) -> np.ndarray:
    """Weights for a 1D panel, same next-open convention as build_weights."""
    return build_weights(tsd, np.zeros((len(tsd), 3)), np.zeros((len(tsd), 3)), p)

# Metrics

def _daily_returns(r: dict):
    dates = bt.session_dates(r["ts"])
    _, last = bt.day_bounds_from_dates(dates)
    eq = r["equity"][last]
    idx = pd.DatetimeIndex(pd.to_datetime(dates[last]))
    return pd.Series(np.diff(eq) / eq[:-1], index=idx[1:]), eq, idx


def _path_stats(rets: pd.Series) -> dict:
    eq = np.r_[1.0, np.cumprod(1.0 + rets.to_numpy(float))]
    years = (rets.index[-1] - rets.index[0]).days / 365.25
    if years <= 0 or eq[-1] <= 0:
        return dict(cagr=None, max_drawdown=None, sharpe=None)
    dd = -(eq / np.maximum.accumulate(eq) - 1.0).min()
    sd = float(rets.std(ddof=0))
    return dict(
        cagr=_f(eq[-1] ** (1.0 / years) - 1.0),
        max_drawdown=_f(dd),
        sharpe=_f(float(rets.mean()) / sd * np.sqrt(252.0)) if sd > 0 else None,
    )


def metrics(ts, o, c, W, start: str = DEV_START, slip: float = 1.0,
            bars: float = BARS_1M) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
    r = bt.run(ts, o, c, W, start=start, band=BAND, slippage_bps=slip)
    s = bt.stats(r, bars)
    i0 = bt.start_index(ts, start)
    w = np.asarray(W[i0:, 1], dtype=float)

    dret, deq, ddates = _daily_returns(r)
    _, _, last = bt.day_bounds(r["ts"])
    tq = c[i0:, 1][last]
    tr = np.diff(tq) / tq[:-1]
    corr = float(np.corrcoef(dret.to_numpy(float), tr)[0, 1]) if len(tr) > 2 else 0.0

    eq = r["equity"]
    peak = np.maximum.accumulate(eq)
    dd = eq / peak - 1.0
    tr_i = int(np.argmin(dd))
    pk_i = int(np.argmax(eq[:tr_i + 1]))
    worst = dret.nsmallest(5)

    yearly = {}
    prev_s = float(deq[0])
    prev_t = float(tq[0])
    for y in sorted(set(ddates.year)):
        m = ddates.year == y
        es = float(deq[m][-1])
        et = float(tq[m][-1])
        yearly[str(int(y))] = {"strategy": _f(es / prev_s - 1.0),
                               "tqqq": _f(et / prev_t - 1.0)}
        prev_s, prev_t = es, et

    out = dict(
        cagr=_f(s["cagr"]),
        max_drawdown=_f(s["max_drawdown"]),
        sharpe=_f(s["sharpe"]),
        sortino=_f(s["sortino"]),
        volatility=_f(s["volatility"]),
        calmar=_f(s["cagr"] / s["max_drawdown"]) if s["max_drawdown"] > 0 else None,
        tqqq_exposure=_f(np.mean(w)),
        min_weight=_f(np.min(w)),
        pct_full=_f(np.mean(w >= 0.99)),
        pct_below_80=_f(np.mean(w < 0.80)),
        pct_below_50=_f(np.mean(w < 0.50)),
        fills=int(s["fills"]),
        turnover=_f(s["turnover"]),
        corr_tqqq=corr,
        max_dd_peak=str(ts[i0:][pk_i])[:19],
        max_dd_trough=str(ts[i0:][tr_i])[:19],
        ending_equity=_f(s["ending_equity"]),
        years=_f(s["years"]),
        yearly=yearly,
        worst_days={str(d.date()): _f(v) for d, v in worst.items()},
    )
    return out, r


def daily_marks(tsd, od, cd, p: dict, slip: float = 1.0) -> dict:
    W = daily_panel_weights(tsd, p)
    m, _ = metrics(tsd, od, cd, W, slip=slip, bars=BARS_1D)
    return {k: m[k] for k in ("cagr", "max_drawdown", "sharpe", "tqqq_exposure")}


def slice_metrics(r: dict, a: str, b: str) -> dict:
    m = (r["ts"] >= _ts(a)) & (r["ts"] < _ts(b))
    e = r["equity"][m]
    t = r["ts"][m]
    if len(e) < 2:
        return {}
    years = (t[-1] - t[0]).total_seconds() / (365.25 * 86400.0)
    rets = np.diff(e) / e[:-1]
    sd = float(np.std(rets))
    return dict(
        cagr=_f((e[-1] / e[0]) ** (1.0 / years) - 1.0) if e[0] > 0 else None,
        max_drawdown=_f(float(-(e / np.maximum.accumulate(e) - 1.0).min())),
        sharpe=_f(float(np.mean(rets)) / sd * np.sqrt(BARS_1M)) if sd > 0 else None,
        years=_f(years),
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Placebos
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def placebo_block(tsd, od, cd, w_dev: np.ndarray, real_stats: dict,
                  n_draws: int = 500, seed: int = 7) -> dict:
    n = len(tsd)
    const = float(np.mean(w_dev))
    Wc = np.zeros((n, 3))
    Wc[:, 1] = const
    Wc[:, 2] = 1.0 - const
    rc = bt.run(tsd, od, cd, Wc, start=DEV_START, band=BAND, slippage_bps=1.0)
    const_stats = _path_stats(_daily_returns(rc)[0])

    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    shifts = rng.integers(60, n - 60, size=n_draws)
    Wlist = []
    for k in shifts:
        Wk = np.zeros((n, 3))
        wk = np.roll(w_dev, int(k))
        Wk[:, 1] = wk
        Wk[:, 2] = 1.0 - wk
        Wlist.append(Wk)
    results = bt.run_many(tsd, od, cd, Wlist, start=DEV_START, band=BAND,
                          slippage_bps=1.0, threads=1)
    pstats = [_path_stats(_daily_returns(x)[0]) for x in results]
    pc = np.array([s["cagr"] for s in pstats], dtype=float)
    pdd = np.array([s["max_drawdown"] for s in pstats], dtype=float)
    ps = np.array([s["sharpe"] for s in pstats], dtype=float)

    lags = {}
    for k in (5, 20, 60):
        wk = np.r_[np.full(k, w_dev[0]), w_dev[:-k]]
        Wk = np.zeros((n, 3))
        Wk[:, 1] = wk
        Wk[:, 2] = 1.0 - wk
        rk = bt.run(tsd, od, cd, Wk, start=DEV_START, band=BAND,
                    slippage_bps=1.0)
        lags[str(k)] = _path_stats(_daily_returns(rk)[0])

    return dict(
        marks="daily",
        matched_constant=dict(weight=_f(const), **const_stats),
        circular_shift=dict(
            draws=int(n_draws),
            cagr_mean=_f(pc.mean()),
            cagr_p05=_f(np.percentile(pc, 5)),
            cagr_p50=_f(np.percentile(pc, 50)),
            cagr_p95=_f(np.percentile(pc, 95)),
            dd_mean=_f(pdd.mean()),
            dd_p50=_f(np.percentile(pdd, 50)),
            sharpe_p50=_f(np.percentile(ps, 50)),
            frac_cagr_ge_real=_f(np.mean(pc >= real_stats["cagr"])),
            frac_both_ge_real=_f(np.mean(
                (pc >= real_stats["cagr"])
                & (pdd <= real_stats["max_drawdown"]))),
        ),
        lag=lags,
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Main
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def main() -> None:
    print("loading panels (development window only)", flush=True)
    ts1, o1, c1 = bt.panel(SYMS, DEV_START, DEV_END, "1min", warmup_days=0)
    tsd, od, cd = bt.panel(SYMS, DEV_START, DEV_END, "1D", warmup_days=0)
    i1 = bt.start_index(ts1, DEV_START)
    print(f"  1m {len(ts1):,} bars  {ts1[0]} .. {ts1[-1]}", flush=True)
    print(f"  1d {len(tsd):,} bars  {tsd[0]} .. {tsd[-1]}", flush=True)

    bench = dict(
        tqqq_1m=bt.benchmark(c1[i1:, 1], ts1[i1:], BARS_1M),
        tqqq_1d=bt.benchmark(cd[:, 1], tsd, BARS_1D),
        qqq_1m=bt.benchmark(c1[i1:, 0], ts1[i1:], BARS_1M),
    )
    for k, v in bench.items():
        print(f"  bench {k}: CAGR {v['cagr']*100:.2f}%  DD {v['max_drawdown']*100:.2f}%"
              f"  Sharpe {v['sharpe']:.2f}", flush=True)

    # ---- pre-registered grid ------------------------------------------------
    print("\n== grid (8 cells, 1m marks, 1 bp) ==", flush=True)
    grid = {}
    Wcand = rcand = rdcand = wd_cand = None
    for name, p in GRID.items():
        W = build_weights(ts1, o1, c1, p)
        m, r = metrics(ts1, o1, c1, W, slip=1.0)
        m["daily_marks_1bp"] = daily_marks(tsd, od, cd, p)
        grid[name] = m
        print(f"  {name:16s} CAGR {m['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {m['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%"
              f"  Sharpe {m['sharpe']:4.2f}  TQQQ {m['tqqq_exposure']*100:5.1f}%"
              f"  fills {m['fills']:,}", flush=True)
        if name == CANDIDATE:
            Wcand, rcand = W, r
            wd_cand = daily_weights(load_daily(DEV_END), p)

    cand = grid[CANDIDATE]
    costs = {}
    for slip in (5.0, 10.0):
        costs[f"{int(slip)}bp"], _ = metrics(ts1, o1, c1, Wcand, slip=slip)
    print(f"  candidate 5bp  CAGR {costs['5bp']['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD "
          f"{costs['5bp']['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%", flush=True)
    print(f"  candidate 10bp CAGR {costs['10bp']['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD "
          f"{costs['10bp']['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%", flush=True)

    # ---- plateau ------------------------------------------------------------
    passing = [k for k, m in grid.items()
               if m["cagr"] > BAR_CAGR and m["max_drawdown"] < BAR_DD]
    dd60 = [k for k, m in grid.items() if m["max_drawdown"] < 0.60]
    cagrs = [m["cagr"] for m in grid.values()]
    dds = [m["max_drawdown"] for m in grid.values()]
    best_cagr = max(grid, key=lambda k: grid[k]["cagr"])
    plateau = dict(
        cells=len(grid),
        passing=len(passing),
        passing_ids=passing,
        meets_dd60_ids=dd60,
        cagr_min=_f(min(cagrs)),
        cagr_max=_f(max(cagrs)),
        dd_min=_f(min(dds)),
        dd_max=_f(max(dds)),
        primary_is_best_cagr=(best_cagr == PRIMARY),
        candidate_is_best_cagr=(best_cagr == CANDIDATE),
        best_cagr_id=best_cagr,
        candidate=dict(cagr=cand["cagr"], max_drawdown=cand["max_drawdown"]),
        pre_registered_primary=dict(cagr=cand["cagr"],
                                    max_drawdown=cand["max_drawdown"]),
    )
    print(f"\n  plateau: {len(passing)}/{len(grid)} pass  "
          f"CAGR {plateau['cagr_min']*100:.2f}-{plateau['cagr_max']*100:.2f}%  "
          f"DD {plateau['dd_min']*100:.2f}-{plateau['dd_max']*100:.2f}%", flush=True)

    # ---- neighbours ---------------------------------------------------------
    print("\n== neighbours (1m marks, 1 bp) ==", flush=True)
    neighbours = {}
    for name, p in {**TARGET_SWEEP, **ESTIMATOR_SWEEP, **BRAKE_SWEEP,
                    **SMOOTH_SWEEP}.items():
        W = build_weights(ts1, o1, c1, p)
        m, _ = metrics(ts1, o1, c1, W, slip=1.0)
        neighbours[name] = m
        print(f"  {name:14s} CAGR {m['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {m['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%"
              f"  Sharpe {m['sharpe']:4.2f}  TQQQ {m['tqqq_exposure']*100:5.1f}%", flush=True)

    # ---- binary and vol-acceleration cut rivals ------------------------------
    print("\n== cut-shape rivals (1m marks, 1 bp) ==", flush=True)
    rivals = {}
    df_sig = load_daily(DEV_END)
    vol20 = estimate_vol(df_sig, "rv", 20)
    lr = np.log(df_sig["close"]).diff()
    rv5 = lr.rolling(5).std(ddof=1) * np.sqrt(252.0)
    base_series = np.minimum(0.80 / vol20.to_numpy(float), 1.0)
    base_series = np.where(np.isfinite(base_series), base_series, 0.0)
    hi15 = df_sig["close"].rolling(15).max()
    dd15 = (1.0 - df_sig["close"] / hi15).to_numpy(float)
    brake_bin = np.where(dd15 >= 0.12, 0.25, 1.0)
    brake_acc = np.where((rv5.to_numpy(float) > 1.5 * vol20.to_numpy(float))
                         & (rv5.to_numpy(float) > 0.70), 0.30, 1.0)
    for name, brake in (("binary_dd12", brake_bin), ("volaccel", brake_acc)):
        w = pd.Series(base_series * brake, index=df_sig.index)
        w = w.ewm(span=SMOOTH, adjust=False).mean()
        W = build_weights(ts1, o1, c1, dict(BASE))
        # replace the TQQQ weight with this rival series via the same mapping
        wm = pd.Series(w, index=df_sig.index)
        dates, first, last = bt.day_bounds(ts1)
        sess = pd.DatetimeIndex(pd.to_datetime(dates[last]))
        at = wm.reindex(sess, method="ffill")
        prev = at.shift(1)
        before = wm[wm.index < sess[0]]
        prev.iloc[0] = float(before.iloc[-1]) if len(before) else 0.0
        wb = np.repeat(prev.to_numpy(float), last - first + 1)
        wb = np.roll(wb, -1)
        wb[-1] = prev.to_numpy(float)[-1]
        W[:, 1] = np.clip(wb, 0.0, 1.0)
        W[:, 2] = 1.0 - W[:, 1]
        m, _ = metrics(ts1, o1, c1, W, slip=1.0)
        rivals[name] = m
        print(f"  {name:14s} CAGR {m['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD {m['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%"
              f"  Sharpe {m['sharpe']:4.2f}  TQQQ {m['tqqq_exposure']*100:5.1f}%", flush=True)

    # ---- constant blends ----------------------------------------------------
    print("\n== constant TQQQ blends ==", flush=True)
    blends = {}
    n1 = len(ts1)
    for b in BLENDS:
        W = np.zeros((n1, 3))
        W[:, 1] = b
        W[:, 2] = 1.0 - b
        m, _ = metrics(ts1, o1, c1, W, slip=1.0)
        blends[f"{int(round(b*100))}pct"] = m
        print(f"  {int(round(b*100)):3d}% TQQQ  CAGR {m['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  "
              f"DD {m['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  Sharpe {m['sharpe']:4.2f}", flush=True)

    # ---- placebos -----------------------------------------------------------
    print("\n== placebos (daily marks, 500 circular shifts) ==", flush=True)
    dates_d = pd.DatetimeIndex(pd.to_datetime(bt.session_dates(tsd)))
    w_dev = wd_cand.reindex(dates_d, method="ffill").to_numpy(float)
    w_dev = np.where(np.isfinite(w_dev), w_dev, 0.0)
    r_daily = bt.run(tsd, od, cd, daily_panel_weights(tsd, BASE),
                     start=DEV_START, band=BAND, slippage_bps=1.0)
    real_daily = _path_stats(_daily_returns(r_daily)[0])
    placebo = placebo_block(tsd, od, cd, w_dev, real_daily)
    placebo["real"] = real_daily
    cs = placebo["circular_shift"]
    print(f"  real daily {real_daily}", flush=True)
    print(f"  matched constant {placebo['matched_constant']}", flush=True)
    print(f"  circular shift {cs}", flush=True)
    print(f"  lag {placebo['lag']}", flush=True)

    # ---- cut tests ----------------------------------------------------------
    print("\n== cut tests ==", flush=True)
    causal = {}
    for cut in CUT_TS:
        j = int(ts1.searchsorted(_ts(cut)))
        Wp = build_weights(ts1[:j], o1[:j], c1[:j], GRID[CANDIDATE])
        diff_m = float(np.max(np.abs(Wp - Wcand[:j]))) if j else 0.0
        jd = int(tsd.searchsorted(_ts(cut).normalize()))
        Wdp = daily_panel_weights(tsd[:jd], GRID[CANDIDATE])
        Wdf = daily_panel_weights(tsd, GRID[CANDIDATE])
        # The last daily bar carries the next session's target; a panel cut at
        # that session cannot contain that target, so compare all earlier bars.
        diff_d = (float(np.max(np.abs(Wdp[:-1] - Wdf[:jd - 1])))
                  if jd > 1 else 0.0)
        causal[cut] = dict(minute_bars=j, minute_max_abs_diff=_f(diff_m),
                           daily_dates=jd, daily_max_abs_diff=_f(diff_d),
                           pass_=bool(diff_m <= 1e-12 and diff_d <= 1e-12))
        print(f"  causal {cut}: {causal[cut]}", flush=True)

    dret, _, _ = _daily_returns(rcand)
    perf_cuts = {}
    for label, year in (("ex_best_year", None), ("ex_2020", 2020), ("ex_2022", 2022)):
        r2 = dret.copy()
        if label == "ex_best_year":
            yrs = sorted(set(dret.index.year))
            by = {y: float((1.0 + dret[dret.index.year == y]).prod() - 1.0)
                  for y in yrs}
            best = max(by, key=by.get)
            r2[dret.index.year == best] = 0.0
            perf_cuts[label] = dict(year=int(best), year_return=_f(by[best]),
                                    **{k: v for k, v in _path_stats(r2).items()})
        else:
            r2[dret.index.year == year] = 0.0
            perf_cuts[label] = _path_stats(r2)
    r2 = dret.copy()
    r2[dret.nlargest(20).index] = 0.0
    perf_cuts["ex_best_20_sessions"] = _path_stats(r2)
    for label in ("ex_2020", "ex_2022", "ex_best_20_sessions"):
        print(f"  {label}: {perf_cuts[label]}", flush=True)
    print(f"  {perf_cuts['ex_best_year']}", flush=True)

    starts = {}
    for s in ("2017-01-03", "2018-01-02"):
        m, _ = metrics(ts1, o1, c1, Wcand, start=s, slip=1.0)
        starts[s] = {k: m[k] for k in ("cagr", "max_drawdown", "sharpe",
                                       "tqqq_exposure")}
        print(f"  start {s}: CAGR {m['cagr']*100:.2f}%  DD "
              f"{m['max_drawdown']*100:.2f}%", flush=True)

    # ---- subperiods and episodes -------------------------------------------
    sub = {}
    for label, a, b in (("2016_19", "2016-01-04", "2020-01-01"),
                        ("2020_21", "2020-01-01", "2022-01-01"),
                        ("2022_23", "2022-01-01", "2023-12-30")):
        sub[label] = slice_metrics(rcand, a, b)

    eps = {}
    _, deq_p, ddates_p = _daily_returns(rcand)
    deq_p = pd.Series(deq_p, index=ddates_p)
    dfw = load_daily(DEV_END)
    for label, a, b in EPISODES:
        wseg = wd_cand.loc[a:b]
        row = dict(avg_weight=_f(wseg.mean()) if len(wseg) else None,
                   min_weight=_f(wseg.min()) if len(wseg) else None,
                   max_weight=_f(wseg.max()) if len(wseg) else None)
        row["tqqq_return"] = _f(float(dfw["close"].loc[b] / dfw["close"].loc[a] - 1.0))
        row["strategy_return"] = _f(float(deq_p.loc[:b].iloc[-1]
                                          / deq_p.loc[:a].iloc[-1] - 1.0))
        eps[label] = row
    print("\n== episodes ==", flush=True)
    for k, v in eps.items():
        print(f"  {k}: strat {v['strategy_return']*100:7.2f}%  "
              f"TQQQ {v['tqqq_return']*100:7.2f}%  avg w {v['avg_weight']*100:5.1f}%",
              flush=True)

    # ---- diagnostics --------------------------------------------------------
    _, deq_d, ddates_d = _daily_returns(rcand)
    _, _, last_d = bt.day_bounds(rcand["ts"])
    tq_d = c1[i1:, 1][last_d]
    tr_d = np.diff(tq_d) / tq_d[:-1]
    sr_d = dret.to_numpy(float)
    up_d, dn_d = tr_d > 0, tr_d < 0
    s_eq = pd.Series(deq_d, index=ddates_d)
    t_eq = pd.Series(tq_d, index=ddates_d)
    sm = s_eq.resample("ME").last().pct_change().dropna()
    tm = t_eq.resample("ME").last().pct_change().dropna()
    vol_c = estimate_vol(dfw, "rv", 20).reindex(wd_cand.index)
    vol_c = vol_c.loc[DEV_START:DEV_END]
    wd_q = wd_cand.loc[DEV_START:DEV_END]
    qq = pd.qcut(vol_c, 5, labels=False)
    quint = [
        dict(q=int(k), vol_min=_f(vol_c[qq == k].min()),
             vol_max=_f(vol_c[qq == k].max()),
             avg_weight=_f(wd_q[qq == k].mean()),
             n=int((qq == k).sum()))
        for k in range(5)
    ]
    key_dates = {
        dt: dict(vol=_f(vol_c.loc[dt]), weight=_f(wd_cand.loc[dt]))
        for dt in ("2020-02-19", "2020-03-12", "2020-03-23", "2020-04-30",
                   "2021-11-19", "2022-01-03", "2022-06-16", "2022-10-14",
                   "2022-12-28", "2023-01-03", "2023-12-29")
    }
    ep = (pd.Timestamp("2021-11-19"), pd.Timestamp("2023-01-06"))
    dd_ep = dict(
        strategy=_f(float(s_eq.loc[ep[0]:ep[1]].min()
                          / s_eq.loc[ep[0]:ep[1]].cummax().max() - 1.0)),
        tqqq=_f(float(t_eq.loc[ep[0]:ep[1]].min()
                      / t_eq.loc[ep[0]:ep[1]].cummax().max() - 1.0)),
    )
    diag = dict(
        beta_daily=_f(np.polyfit(tr_d, sr_d, 1)[0]),
        corr_daily=_f(np.corrcoef(sr_d, tr_d)[0, 1]),
        vol_strategy_daily=_f(np.std(sr_d, ddof=0) * np.sqrt(252.0)),
        vol_tqqq_daily=_f(np.std(tr_d, ddof=0) * np.sqrt(252.0)),
        up_capture_daily=_f(sr_d[up_d].mean() / tr_d[up_d].mean()),
        down_capture_daily=_f(sr_d[dn_d].mean() / tr_d[dn_d].mean()),
        beta_monthly=_f(np.polyfit(tm, sm, 1)[0]) if len(tm) > 2 else None,
        corr_monthly=_f(np.corrcoef(sm, tm)[0, 1]) if len(tm) > 2 else None,
        up_capture_monthly=_f(sm[sm > 0].mean() / tm[tm > 0].mean()) if (tm > 0).any() else None,
        down_capture_monthly=_f(sm[sm < 0].mean() / tm[tm < 0].mean()) if (tm < 0).any() else None,
        weight_by_vol_quintile=quint,
        key_dates=key_dates,
        dd_2021_11_19_2023_01_06=dd_ep,
        tqqq_yearly={int(y): float(v["tqqq"]) for y, v in cand["yearly"].items()},
        tqqq_ex_2020_cagr=_f(_path_stats(
            pd.Series(tr_d, index=dret.index).where(
                dret.index.year != 2020, 0.0))["cagr"]),
        tqqq_ex_2023_cagr=_f(_path_stats(
            pd.Series(tr_d, index=dret.index).where(
                dret.index.year != 2023, 0.0))["cagr"]),
    )
    full_years = (pd.Timestamp(FULL_END) - pd.Timestamp(FULL_START)).days / 365.25
    hold_years = (pd.Timestamp(FULL_END) - pd.Timestamp(HOLD_START)).days / 365.25
    dev_mult = (1.0 + cand["cagr"]) ** float(cand["years"])
    full_mult = (1.0 + FULL_BAR_CAGR) ** full_years
    diag["required_holdout_cagr_to_match_full_bar"] = _f(
        (full_mult / dev_mult) ** (1.0 / hold_years) - 1.0)
    diag["dev_years"] = _f(cand["years"])
    diag["dev_growth_multiple"] = _f(dev_mult)
    diag["full_bar_years"] = _f(full_years)
    diag["full_bar_multiple"] = _f(full_mult)
    diag["holdout_years"] = _f(hold_years)

    # ---- verdict ------------------------------------------------------------
    verdict = dict(
        bar_cagr=BAR_CAGR,
        bar_max_drawdown=BAR_DD,
        bar_sharpe=BAR_SHARPE,
        passes_bar=bool(cand["cagr"] > BAR_CAGR and cand["max_drawdown"] < BAR_DD),
        meets_dd_target=bool(cand["max_drawdown"] < 0.60),
        cagr_minus_bar_pp=_f((cand["cagr"] - BAR_CAGR) * 100.0),
        dd_minus_bar_pp=_f((cand["max_drawdown"] - BAR_DD) * 100.0),
        status="dev_pass" if (cand["cagr"] > BAR_CAGR
                              and cand["max_drawdown"] < 0.60) else "dev_partial",
        promoted_cell=CANDIDATE,
        pre_registered_primary_cell=PRIMARY,
        primary_is_best_cagr=plateau["primary_is_best_cagr"],
        candidate_is_best_cagr=plateau["candidate_is_best_cagr"],
        best_cagr_id=plateau["best_cagr_id"],
        five_bp_pass=bool(costs["5bp"]["cagr"] > BAR_CAGR
                          and costs["5bp"]["max_drawdown"] < 0.60),
        ten_bp_pass=bool(costs["10bp"]["cagr"] > BAR_CAGR
                         and costs["10bp"]["max_drawdown"] < 0.60),
    )

    result = dict(
        agent="tqqq-vol-target-aggressive",
        status=verdict["status"],
        window=dict(start=DEV_START, end=DEV_END,
                    sessions=int(len(tsd)),
                    marks="1-minute", fills="next-open", band=BAND),
        rules=dict(
            weight="EMA_3(clip(target_vol/sigma_t,0,1) * brake_t)",
            brake="clip(1-(dd15-0.06)/(0.12-0.06),0.25,1)",
            remainder="BIL",
            no_trend_filter=True,
            no_slow_gate=True,
            signal_lag="close t -> open t+1",
            candidate=dict(**{k: v for k, v in GRID[CANDIDATE].items()}),
            pre_registered_primary=dict(**{k: v for k, v in GRID[PRIMARY].items()}),
        ),
        verdict=verdict,
        candidate=dict(
            params={k: v for k, v in GRID[CANDIDATE].items()},
            **{"1bp": cand, "5bp": costs["5bp"], "10bp": costs["10bp"]},
        ),
        pre_registered_primary=dict(
            params={k: v for k, v in GRID[PRIMARY].items()},
            **{"1bp": grid[PRIMARY]},
        ),
        grid=grid,
        plateau=plateau,
        neighbours=neighbours,
        cut_rivals=rivals,
        constant_blends=blends,
        placebos=placebo,
        cut_tests=dict(causal=causal, performance=perf_cuts, starts=starts),
        subperiods=sub,
        episodes=eps,
        diagnostics=diag,
        benchmarks=bench,
        notes=[
            "Development window only; 2024-2026 is not read by the dev runner.",
            "The primary rv20_t080 is also the best CAGR cell; the 0.90/1.00 "
            "grid neighbours still pass the program bar, but the DD<60 target "
            "is met with margin only at 0.80.",
            "The fast crash brake is a 15-session drawdown scaler, not a slow "
            "trend gate; it is active often and costs upside in recoveries.",
            "bt.stats 'exposure' is ~1 because BIL is an asset; tqqq_exposure "
            "is the economic TQQQ weight.",
            "Pre-2016 daily bars (2015-01-02 onward) warm the estimators only.",
        ],
    )
    (HERE / "result.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(result, indent=1, default=float), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"\nwrote {HERE / 'result.json'}", flush=True)
